rows.theorem: Lucas theorem for binomial coefficients modulo a prime, together with the Chinese Remainder Theorem
rows.local_check: The four moduli are distinct primes; the base-p expansions of 2002 are correct; adding p^d preserves all digits used by Lucas when d is the digit count; the product of the four periods is a common period modulo 2002.

rows.theorem: For irrational alpha, the fractional parts of n alpha are dense (indeed equidistributed) in [0,1]
rows.local_check: alpha=log_2(3/2) is irrational by unique factorization, and every tail of an irrational rotation is dense, so arbitrarily large n can be chosen in the required interval.
rows.first_problem_after_verification: n13: floor(2^k 2^theta) need not equal 2^k; the omitted factor 2^k invalidates the claimed fractional-part formula.

rows.theorem: Bertrand postulate: for every integer p greater than 1 there is a prime q with p<q<2p
rows.local_check: For consecutive primes p<q, Bertrand gives q<2p. Hence p<m<q implies p<m<2p, so p cannot divide m. The claim at n35 is correct only after this bridge is supplied.

rows.theorem: Senge-Straus/Stewart digit-sum theorem: if a and b are multiplicatively independent integers at least 2, then the base-b digit sum of a^k tends to infinity
rows.local_check: 3 and 5 are multiplicatively independent, so both s_3(5^k) and s_5(3^k) tend to infinity. The named theorem is specialized but explicitly invoked.
rows.first_problem_after_verification: n21: replacing a floor by its argument asserts a false equality; the conclusion can be repaired because the floor error is bounded by 1.

rows.theorem: Edge-isoperimetric upper bound for finite induced subgraphs of the square grid
rows.local_check: For 100 selected grid points, horizontal edges are at most 100-r and vertical edges at most 100-c, where r,c are the nonempty row and column counts. Since rc>=100, r+c>=20, so the total is at most 180; the 10 by 10 construction attains it.

rows.theorem: Gauss-Dirichlet composition of primitive integral binary quadratic forms of a fixed discriminant
rows.local_check: The proof establishes primitiveness and equal discriminant -20 before invoking composition. The main product-closure argument through n55 is supported, but the later claim 5=1^2+5(1)^2 at n65 is arithmetically false (the right side is 6).
